content: Sun & Rain Works holds a private archive relating to its 2009 engagement with Sotheby's Photographs (sale N08533) and the associated conceptual works (The Auction as Artwork, WTF is Ansel Adams, and www.wtfisart.com). The archive is reported to contain 2008 correspondence with Sotheby's (outbound and inbound), records of the consignment of an Ansel Adams photograph, 'San Francisco from Twin Peaks' (lot 16), domain-registration and hosting receipts for www.wtfisart.com, art-referential documentation photographs, and file metadata. Those receipts are now held and examined, and the hosting-receipts record sets them out: they are the registrar's own business records, they date the domain and its hosting to 2009-03-16, and their 'Bill To' block names Sun and Rain Works on every invoice in the run. An earlier version of this record stated the opposite, on a misreading of the registrar's comma-separated export; that statement is withdrawn. These materials evidence the artist identity, the 2008-2009 engagement with Sotheby's, the consignment, contemporaneous conceptual intent, and the public continuity of the 'WTF is Art' concept. They do not, by themselves, record a publicly witnessed live-creation event, and they establish no precedence over any later event. The fuller archive remains held by the studio pending redaction and rights review; no checksums, file hashes, or custody identifiers are published at this time.

referred_to_by.content: Evidence status: mixed. Independently verifiable: (1) the public Sotheby's catalogue lot (sale N08533, lot 16) at https://www.sothebys.com/en/auctions/ecatalogue/2009/photographs-n08533/lot.16.html ; (2) two Sun and Rain Works public posts carrying the 'WTF is Art' theme, both still live on the account when checked on 2026-09-10, and each dated independently by the platform's timestamp-encoded identifier. The earlier reads '#WTF is #Art ?!?!?!' (X post 372900008367894529). Its identifier decodes to 2013-08-29T01:54:24Z, and the platform's own embed gives August 29, 2013. The studio's screenshot of the post shows Aug 28, 2013, because a displayed date is rendered in the viewer's timezone, and 01:54 UTC on 29 August is still 28 August in every timezone from UTC minus two westward, which includes all of the Americas. The later reads '#WTF is #Art ?!' (X post 373257603108704256). Its identifier decodes to 2013-08-30T01:35:22Z, and the embed gives August 30, 2013. The two were posted 23 hours and 41 minutes apart. Neither is assigned a local day here: nothing in this collection places the studio in a particular timezone in 2013. An earlier version of this passage dated the second post to 2013-08-29 by taking Hawaii-Aleutian time as the studio's local time; that assumption is withdrawn. Held privately by the studio: the 2008-2009 correspondence, receipts, and photographs. Selected private items can be promoted to public evidence as redaction and rights review are completed.

The consignment engagement is corroborated by inbound 2008 correspondence from Sotheby's Photographs (confirming intake logistics and naming the department administrator) and by a shared Hana, HI mailing address linking the consignor to the Sun & Rain Works domain receipts. Contemporaneous conceptual intent is evidenced by art-referential documentation (an Andy Warhol volume juxtaposed with the photograph in images sent to Sotheby's). Each item is scoped to what it shows: these evidence identity, consignment, intent, and the concept's public continuity — not a witnessed live-creation event, and not precedence over any later artist or event.

Part of the documentation described here has since been dated and published as a record in its own right. The art-referential documentation photographs — including the frame composing the print with a volume of Warhol's philosophy — carry camera-written Exif placing them on 2008-08-08, and their close-up of the print's verso agrees in four particulars with the public Sotheby's catalogue entry for lot 16. That material is no longer only studio-reported: see the documentation-photograph evidence record.

referred_to_by.content: The catalogue entry, captured and checked, and a gap that remains open. This collection calls the public catalogue entry for lot 16 its independently verifiable anchor, and thirteen records rely on it - for the sale date, the lot and title, the 1952 dating, the verso particulars against which the documentation photographs are tested, the estimate, and five times over for what it does not say, which is that it does not name Sun and Rain Works. Until now it was held as a live URL and nothing else. It has been fetched, and what it said on the date of fetching is now fixed: the page, its byte count and its SHA-256 are recorded in a manifest under data/evidence/, together with a transcription of the particulars the records depend on. The page itself is third-party commercial content and is not republished. Three things were confirmed at capture. The verso description matches the studio's photographs, including the frame in which the whole inscription is legible. The estimate of 7,000 to 10,000 US dollars matches the figure the auction house gave in its message of 2008-08-15, so that figure now has two independent sources. And the entry names no consignor, so the negative statement this collection repeats is true of the page as fetched. One detail is new: the catalogue attributes the 'Wells Fargo Bank' annotation to Adams himself. The gap that remains is this, and it is sharper than it first appeared. The Internet Archive holds no capture of lot 16, in any form: a query matching the lot path with any query string returns an empty set, and the availability and direct-timestamp methods return nothing and a 404. But the catalogue around it is archived. The same sale has been crawled from 2016 to 2025, ten of its lots have some capture and seven have a successful one, among them lots 27, 44, 61, 73 and 78; the locale-qualified form of these URLs is crawled too, lot 27 having been taken twice in that form. So the archive reaches this catalogue and has done for nine years. Lot 16 is a hole in covered ground, which is a more specific fact than an unarchived site and a smaller thing to fix. An attempt to create one was refused: Save Page Now returned a 401 and the message that a login is required, anonymous archiving having been withdrawn. The publisher is not the obstacle - the site's robots.txt disallows only the lot PDF and carries no archiver exclusion. So the anchor still rests on a commercial page staying online, and the capture made here is the studio's own and is not independent. A logged-in archive.org account would close this in one step, and the manifest records what to add when it is done. A note on the address, since two forms of it circulate. The page answers both at the bare lot path and with a locale=en query appended, and on the capture date the two served byte-identical content, the same 42,070 bytes under the same SHA-256. Either may be cited and the checksum recorded here covers both.
